verdicts.reason: A: the white card fills almost the whole canvas, so the desert dunes that carry the original's mood shrink to a thin strip at the bottom. A huge empty white gap separates the subhead from a tiny See Fares button stranded bottom-left, and the centred logo clashes with the left-aligned copy. B: the card runs off the right edge with no margin, and See Fares is jammed against that edge beside the logo. That puts the CTA above the headline and breaks the reading order. Still, B keeps the text grouped, has a strong headline and shows more of the desert, so it is less broken than A's empty card.
